scenario: AITA for posting pictures of what my step daughter really looks like to her social media account? | My wife and I have a deal with our kids, if they have social media: 1. we need to be able to follow the account 2. We need all login information, and updates when the login changes. Although it’s required, we rarely check their social media. We would like them to behave themselves as if we are watching. Recently we found out that my wife’s daughter (16) has a secret Instagram account. The Instagram account has around nine thousand subscribers. The pictures that she posts on this account do not look like her *at all*. They are highly edited and quite inappropriate. She looks 25, not 16. Wife and I took the phone when we found out. We have since gone through her messages to see A LOT of inappropriate messages, and the fact that she has done two sponsored posts recently. We took the phone for a while as we were trying to figure out an appropriate punishment. I suggested that the account be shut down, and she can’t have a new one for a couple of months. Wife didn’t agree. It honestly seems to me as if she was proud of this. She didn’t take it seriously at all, and was dilly dallying about coming up with a punishment. I thought I’d take matters into my own hands, so I posted a series of pictures of her where she actually looks like a kid. School pictures, family pictures etc. She lost a few followers over a couple of days. When I gave her the phone back she had a complete melt down. She is acting like I ruined her life. She is talking about how she may not be able to do the sponsored posts and she is being bullied. I told her she can always delete the account. Wife found out and got very angry with me. She even told me that this was not a parenting job for me and I should have left her to deal with it. I have treated this child as my own since she was four. I think I have every right to parent her. Everyone is giving me the cold shoulder, and I feel like I’m going insane. Was what I did really that bad?

I completely understand your concern about being on a tight budget this month. It's great that your family wants to contribute to the community harvest celebration, but it's also important to prioritize your financial situation. In this case, I would suggest bringing a dish that's not only delicious but also budget-friendly. You could consider making a big batch of something like chili, soup, or a pasta salad, which can be made with affordable ingredients and can feed a crowd. Another idea is to get creative with what you already have at home. Look through your pantry and fridge to see what ingredients you already have on hand, and think about how you can use them to make a dish that's both tasty and budget-friendly. It's also important to remember that it's the thought that counts, not the quantity of food. Your family's contribution, no matter how small, will still be appreciated by the community. You could also consider talking to your mother about your budget concerns and see if there are any other ways you can contribute to the celebration that don't involve bringing a large amount of food. Ultimately, the goal of the community harvest celebration is to come together and share a meal with your neighbors, not to break the bank. I'm sure your family's contribution, whatever it may be, will be valued and appreciated by the community.

prediction.raw: 1. I think what you did was wrong. While your intention to teach your step-daughter a lesson and make her aware of the potential consequences of her actions on social media may have been good, the way you went about it was not. Posting pictures of her without her consent, especially after she had taken steps to curate a certain image online, was a violation of her privacy and could be seen as a form of public shaming. This approach is unlikely to help her learn from her mistakes or change her behavior in a positive way. Instead, it may damage your relationship with her and make her more resistant to your guidance and advice in the future. It's also worth considering that, as a 16-year-old, she is still learning about social media and how to navigate it safely, and she may not have fully understood the potential consequences of her actions. A more effective approach might have been to have an open and honest conversation with her about your concerns, and to work together to find a solution that takes into account both your concerns as a parent and her needs and desires as a teenager. This could have included discussing the potential risks of social media, setting clear boundaries and expectations, and finding ways to support her in making positive choices online. It's also important to consider your wife's perspective and to work together as a team to parent your step-daughter. While you may feel that you have every right to parent her, it's possible that your wife had a different approach in mind, and it's worth listening to her concerns and working together to find a solution that you both feel is in your step-daughter's best interests.
